# Ten Ideas That Would Make This Starter Exceptional

*2026-07-16 — generated by Claude (Fable 5), grounded in a full inventory of the current codebase. Written independently of the other documents in this directory.*

## How these were chosen

I generated roughly one hundred candidate ideas across twelve categories (type safety & DX, generators, real-time, authorization, auth completeness, data/CRUD ergonomics, notifications & email, observability, data safety, multi-tenancy, billing, AI) and filtered them through four lenses:

1. **Leverage** — value delivered per unit of implementation and maintenance cost, *in this specific codebase*. Ash 3 changes the math on almost everything: resources are declarative and fully introspectable (attributes, types, constraints, actions, policies), so features that would be hand-maintained glue in a vanilla Phoenix app become codegen or configuration here.
2. **Template fit** — every newborn app must benefit. Features an app might not need (billing, teams) lost points; foundations every app uses daily won points.
3. **Ash-native fit** — prefer riding existing machinery (AshOban, AshAdmin, Ash notifiers, `Ash.can?`, ecosystem extensions) over new abstractions.
4. **Complexity honesty** — the repo's whole identity is "pinned, always-green, agent-legible." Anything that would make the gate flakier or the template harder to reason about was cut, no matter how cool.

Effort scale: **S** ≈ a day, **M** ≈ 2–4 days, **L** ≈ a week, for someone who knows the codebase.

---

## 1. The Typed Seam — `mix starter.codegen` from Ash resources to TypeScript, Zod, and route helpers

**What.** A single dev-only mix task that introspects the app and emits `assets/js/generated/`:

- **Resource types** — TypeScript interfaces for the public attributes of every Ash resource (name, type, `allow_nil?`), replacing the hand-maintained `assets/js/types/*.ts` that will drift the moment an agent adds a field.
- **Zod schemas** — Ash validations and constraints (`min_length`, `max_length`, `match`, numeric bounds, `one_of`) map almost one-to-one onto Zod, which is *already in package.json* alongside react-hook-form and `@hookform/resolvers`. Client-side pre-validation with the server as the single source of truth — the classic double-maintenance problem, deleted.
- **Route helpers** — `StarterKitWeb.Router.__routes__()` gives verb, path, and params for every route. Emit a Ziggy-style `routes.ts`: `path("notes.edit", note.id)` with typed params. Today the frontend hardcodes path strings; every renamed route is a silent runtime 404.
- **Shared-prop types** — one generated `SharedProps` interface (`current_user`, `flash`) so `usePage<SharedProps>()` is typed everywhere, matching whatever prop-casing the Inertia config uses.

**Why it wins.** This is the deepest structural weakness of every Inertia app — the untyped seam between server and client — and this repo is uniquely positioned to close it because Ash resources are *data*, not code to parse. It also fits the house style perfectly: `mix starter.codegen --check` joins `ash_postgres.generate_migrations --check` in the `precommit` alias, so drift fails the gate instead of failing in production. For the `--api` flavor, the same story already half-exists: generate a typed client from the OpenAPI spec at `/api/v1/open_api` with `openapi-typescript`.

**Build sketch.** Introspection via `Ash.Resource.Info.public_attributes/1`, `Ash.Resource.Info.actions/1`, and router reflection; a small typemapper (Ash type → TS type → Zod call); deterministic output with a header comment; `--check` compares against committed files. No new runtime deps.

**Effort:** M. **Flavor:** web (API flavor gets the OpenAPI variant). The single highest-leverage idea on this list — and it makes ideas 2, 4, and 5 stronger.

---

## 2. `mix starter.gen.slice` — the demo slice, weaponized as a generator

**What.** An Igniter-powered generator (igniter is already a dev dep) that stamps out a complete vertical slice exactly the shape of the existing Notes demo:

```
mix starter.gen.slice Blog Post title:string body:text --owned
```

produces: Ash domain + resource (owner policies, timestamps, the same patterns as `lib/starter_kit/notes/`), migration via `ash_postgres.generate_migrations`, controller + serializer following `note_controller.ex`, router entries injected by Igniter, React pages (`index.tsx`, `form.tsx`) built from the demo slice's shadcn patterns, generated types (or a `starter.codegen` run, if idea 1 lands), and the full test spread — resource test, controller test, and a tagged Playwright E2E — then runs the gate.

**Why it wins.** The README's stated mission is "AI agents can start shipping features immediately from working, conventional code." The demo slice teaches conventions by example; a generator *enforces* them by construction. It's also the inverse of machinery that already exists: `bin/remove_demo` proves slices are cleanly removable, so slices are already a first-class unit in this repo's mental model. Every generated slice is born green, tested, policy-guarded, and typed. For agents this is the difference between "imitate the demo and hope" and "call one command, then edit working code" — dramatically fewer tokens, dramatically fewer conventions violated.

**Build sketch.** Igniter templates derived by parameterizing the current demo slice files; the demo slice itself becomes the generator's golden fixture (CI births a project, generates a slice, runs the gate).

**Effort:** L (template plumbing is fiddly, but it's mostly transcription of code that already exists). The highest *compounding* payoff here: every future feature in every newborn app flows through it.

---

## 3. Live Props — server-pushed partial reloads via Ash notifiers

**What.** LiveView-grade freshness without leaving Inertia, in three small pieces:

1. Declare `Ash.Notifier.PubSub` on a resource (`pub_sub do publish_all :notes ... end`) — pure configuration, no new code.
2. One authenticated user socket + a thin channel that bridges those PubSub topics to the browser.
3. A React hook: `useLiveProps({ topic: "notes", only: ["notes"] })` that listens and calls `router.reload({ only, async: true })`, debounced.

Edit a note in one tab (or from AshAdmin, or from an Oban job) and every open list updates within a second — fetching only the `notes` prop, through the exact same controller/serializer/policy path as a normal request.

**Why it wins.** This is the sharpest criticism of choosing Inertia over LiveView on a BEAM stack: "you gave up real-time." This answers it with ~150 lines, no client state store, no delta protocol, no second data path — the reload *is* the ordinary request cycle, so authorization and serialization can't drift. Almost no Inertia starter in any ecosystem has this, and Phoenix is the ecosystem best equipped to do it. It also becomes the transport for idea 7 (notifications) and the job-progress pattern (an AshOban trigger completes → publish → the page refetches), so one small investment powers three features.

**Effort:** M. **Flavor:** web only (cleanly inside `PRUNE:WEB`).

---

## 4. Can-Props — policy-aware UI from the policies you already wrote

**What.** Ash policies are the template's authorization brain (with an admin bypass and owner rules already in place) — but the frontend is blind to them, so UIs either show buttons that will 403 or hand-duplicate rules in TypeScript. Fix: a serializer helper that attaches abilities using the real engine:

```elixir
serialize(note, abilities: [:update, :destroy], actor: user)
# => %{id: ..., title: ..., can: %{update: true, destroy: false}}
```

implemented with `Ash.can?/3` (which evaluates the actual policy graph), plus a generated `Can<Resource>` type from idea 1, plus a trivial `can(note, "destroy")` frontend helper.

**Why it wins.** Single source of truth for authorization, extended to the last mile. Buttons, menu items, and empty states now derive from the same SAT-solved policies that guard the action itself — a category of bug (UI/authz drift) eliminated rather than mitigated, for a feature that is nearly free because the policy engine is already there and already queryable. This is the kind of thing that makes people adopt a starter: it feels impossible until you see it, and then it feels obvious.

**Build sketch.** ~50-line helper with an explicit opt-in list of abilities per call site (keeps policy evaluation off hot paths unless asked); document the batch pattern for lists. Honest caveat: data-dependent policies may need their references loaded — the helper should raise loudly in dev when they aren't.

**Effort:** S. Best value-per-line on this list.

---

## 5. Tables That Ship Finished — Ash pagination + a URL-state data-table kit

**What.** Ash read actions support keyset and offset pagination, sorting, and filtering natively — the template just doesn't turn them on (`list_notes` is an unpaginated read, and the gaps list calls it out). Ship the whole vertical once:

- `pagination offset?: true, keyset?: true, default_limit: 25` on list actions.
- A controller-side `paginate_params/1` helper mapping `?page[...]`, `?sort=`, `?q=` to the Ash read, and a `serialize_page/2` returning `{data, meta}`.
- A frontend `useTable()` hook that owns URL state (Inertia partial reloads with `only: ["notes"]`, `preserveState`), plus a shadcn `<DataTable>` with column sorting, a search box, empty states, and pagination controls.
- The demo Notes index converted to it, so the generator (idea 2) stamps it into every future slice.

**Why it wins.** Every application ever built on this template will render filterable lists — it's the single most-repeated UI job in existence, it's tedious to get right (URL state, back-button behavior, preserving scroll, server-driven sort), and the server half is nearly free because Ash already implements it. This is the least glamorous idea in the ten and probably the one users touch most hours per day.

**Effort:** M. **Flavor:** web for the kit; the pagination-on-actions half benefits the JSON:API flavor too (AshJsonApi exposes it automatically).

---

## 6. Identity, Finished — OAuth, TOTP 2FA, device sessions, sudo mode

**What.** The auth foundation is unusually complete (password, magic link, confirmation, reset, remember-me, API keys, token revocation) — finish the story with the four things every serious app adds within a month, as a menu of independent pieces:

- **OAuth** — AshAuthentication ships assent-based strategies (Google, GitHub, OIDC…); this is mostly configuration, a `UserIdentity` resource, and two buttons on `auth/sign-in.tsx`.
- **TOTP 2FA** — NimbleTOTP (tiny, Dashbit) + a secret attribute, QR enrollment in settings, a step-up screen after password sign-in, hashed backup codes.
- **Device sessions UI** — the `Token` resource already stores every issued token (`store_all_tokens?`) and revocation machinery already exists (`log_out_everywhere`). A "Sessions" settings section listing active tokens with created-at/purpose and a revoke button is *mostly UI over data the template already keeps*.
- **Sudo mode** — a `require_recent_auth` plug (re-confirm password/TOTP within N minutes) guarding password change, 2FA changes, and API-key management, GitHub-style.

**Why it wins.** Auth is the one subsystem users are terrified to modify — which is exactly why the template finishing it is worth so much. Each piece is small because the hard parts (token storage, senders, confirmation flows, the settings page) already exist; together they make the newborn's security story genuinely production-grade rather than demo-grade.

**Effort:** S–M per piece; M–L for all four. **Flavor:** both (OAuth/2FA policies apply to API tokens too).

## 7. Notifications That Compound — in-app + email digest on the Live Props bus

**What.** A `Notification` Ash resource (recipient, type, payload map, `read_at`) with a code interface (`notify/3`), a pub_sub notifier so idea 3's hook makes the bell badge update live, a shadcn popover inbox + `/notifications` page, per-user preference toggles, and an AshOban-scheduled digest that emails unread notifications through the existing Swoosh sender pattern — plus an `expire old notifications` trigger mirroring the existing `expire_unconfirmed_users` one.

**Why it wins.** Notifications are the canonical "every app needs it, everyone builds it badly under deadline" subsystem — cross-cutting (DB + realtime + email + preferences + UI), so it's miserable to retrofit but clean to ship in a template where every layer it touches (Ash, Oban triggers, Swoosh senders, Inertia shared props) already has an established pattern to extend. It's also the feature that makes the starter *feel* alive in the first five minutes of a demo.

**Build sketch.** One resource + one trigger + one channel topic + two components; `notify/3` is the whole API surface app code learns.

**Effort:** M (S if idea 3 exists — which is the point).

---

## 8. The Safety Net — soft delete, undo, and audit trail via Ash extensions

**What.** Three ecosystem extensions composed into one trust story:

- **`ash_archival`** on user-facing resources: destroys become archives, reads filter archived rows automatically, and a "Trash" view with restore is a read action + one page. A scheduled AshOban trigger purges archives after 30 days (the `expire_unconfirmed_users` pattern again).
- **Undo toasts**: because deletes are archives, the destroy response can flash an undo token; the flash component grows an action button — "Note deleted · Undo" — that calls unarchive within the grace window. Users stop fearing the delete button.
- **`ash_paper_trail`** on the resources that matter: declarative version history with actor attribution, viewable for free in AshAdmin — an audit log for roughly ten lines of DSL per resource.

**Why it wins.** Data-loss protection is the least sexy, most valuable property a starter can bake in, and it's the kind of thing nobody retrofits until after the incident. Here it's nearly all configuration because the Ash ecosystem already built the hard parts; the template's contribution is composing them, wiring the undo UX, and making the generator (idea 2) apply them by default. "Every newborn app has undo and an audit trail" is a headline feature for the cost of a settings page.

**Effort:** S–M. **Flavor:** both (undo toast is web; archival/audit are domain-level).

---

## 9. The Error Inbox — zero-dependency error tracking with a free UI

**What.** Production error visibility without signing up for anything:

- An `ErrorEvent` Ash resource: fingerprint, kind, message, stacktrace, request context (route, user id, params digest), occurrence count, first/last seen.
- Capture via telemetry/error handlers on the endpoint and Oban (dedupe by fingerprint, increment count) — write-behind so error capture can never take down a request.
- A tiny CSRF-exempt, rate-limited `/client-errors` endpoint + a React `ErrorBoundary` that reports frontend crashes with component stacks — covering the half of an Inertia app that server-side tools never see.
- **UI for free**: it's an Ash resource, so AshAdmin already renders, filters, and sorts it behind the existing admin gate. An AshOban trigger prunes resolved/stale events; optionally, first-occurrence-of-new-fingerprint emails admins through the existing sender pattern.

**Why it wins.** Every newborn app gets Sentry-grade *basics* (what broke, how often, for whom, on both halves of the stack) with zero external services, zero DSNs, zero cost — perfectly aligned with a template whose identity is self-contained and pinned. And because the whole thing is an Ash resource plus handlers, an app that outgrows it can adopt a real APM later without unwinding anything.

**Effort:** M. **Flavor:** both.

---

## 10. The AI Slice — `ash_ai` actions with a streaming chat scaffold

**What.** A demo-slice-sized, removable example of AI done the Ash way:

- Add **`ash_ai`** and define one prompt-backed action on the existing Notes demo — e.g. `summarize` on `Note`, or an "ask your notes" action — so AI calls are actions with policies, typed inputs/outputs, and (via AshOban) background execution and retries, not loose `Task.async` calls to an HTTP client.
- One thin streaming path: a channel that relays tokens, and a `useStream()` hook + minimal chat page in shadcn.
- Because they're Ash actions, the API flavor exposes them through JSON:API automatically, and `ash_ai`'s tool/MCP support means the newborn's *own domain actions* are callable by agents in dev — which is exactly this template's audience.
- Shipped like the Notes slice: worked example, tests with Mimic-mocked providers (no API keys in the gate), and removable by a `bin/remove_ai`-style script.

**Why it wins.** "AI-ready" is the first question asked of any starter in 2026, and most answers are a vendor SDK bolted onto a controller. Running it through Ash actions inherits the template's whole value system — policies, background jobs, testability, API exposure — for free, and teaches agents the *conventional* way to add AI features rather than the ad-hoc way. Scoped as one worked example, not a framework, it stays honest to the complexity budget.

**Effort:** M. **Flavor:** both.

---

## The best ideas that didn't make it

- **Teams/organizations** — the most-requested SaaS capability, and Ash's first-class multitenancy is the right tool; cut because it re-architects every resource, policy, and page in the template. Right shape: an Igniter installer module once idea 2 proves the machinery.
- **Installer-recipe architecture** (`mix starter.install billing|teams|uploads`) — the natural evolution of the birth/prune model; premature before one generator (idea 2) exists.
- **Billing (Stripe)** — high demand, but heavy, external-service-coupled, and not universal. Installer-module material.
- **File uploads (direct-to-S3 + attachments resource)** — solid M-effort candidate; lost the last slot to ideas with more Ash leverage.
- **SSR + SEO kit** — real value for public pages, but adds a Node runtime to deploys; against the always-green ethos for a mostly-behind-login starter.
- **Inertia dev HUD** (per-request prop payload size, query counts, N+1 warnings) — delightful; partially overlaps Tidewave, which the repo already ships for agents.
- **Feature flags, command palette, CSV import wizard, i18n bridge, presence/typing indicators** — all good; all beaten on either universality or leverage.

## The theme, in one sentence

Ash resources are introspectable data, so the highest-leverage features here — generated types, generated slices, policy-aware UIs, free admin surfaces, declarative realtime — are ones every other stack has to hand-write and this template can *derive*.
